tasks.title: Unify issue review API comparison semantics
tasks.description: Refactor the issue review endpoints to compute one shared comparison context for base, head, merge-base, and branch relationship metadata before building diff or commit responses. Make `/api/issues/:number/diff` return merge-base-to-head file changes and make `/api/issues/:number/commits` expose the same semantic metadata so both surfaces describe the same pending merge set.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/issues/:number/diff returns only merge-base-to-head file changes equivalent to `git diff <base>...<head>` when base and issue branches exist
Diff response includes displayable semantic metadata including base, head, mergeBase, ahead, behind, canFastForward, and comparison=merge-base
GET /api/issues/:number/commits returns the pending head-not-in-base commit list together with the same comparison metadata and summary counts aligned with the diff response
Behind-base branches do not include base-only files in diff summary, file list, or per-file patch content
Existing unavailable states for not_started, worktree_removed, branch_missing, and git_error remain explicit and user-displayable
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Prefer a small helper local to the issue review routes that resolves merge-base and reuses WorktreeManager.getWorktreeStatus for ahead/behind/canFastForward. Keep commit-diff endpoint commit-scoped rather than redefining Files changed semantics.

tasks.title: Add merge-framed changes and commits summary to Issue Detail
tasks.description: Update frontend review response types, API client methods, and Issue Detail rendering to consume the new comparison metadata without recomputing semantics in the browser. Render a lightweight merge-framed changes summary plus a first-class commits section with clear empty and unavailable states, and let commit rows navigate to the detailed files reader.
acceptanceCriteria: Frontend review types and query hooks model the new comparison metadata and availability-aware diff/commit payloads
Issue Detail shows merge framing such as `mo/issue-N wants to merge into <base>` together with files changed, additions, deletions, and merge-base semantic copy when review data is available
Issue Detail shows a commits section with commit count, short hash, subject, and relative time or equivalent metadata
Commit rows provide a navigation path into the files page commit view or equivalent commit-specific inspection surface
Not-started, worktree-removed, branch-missing, and git-error states render clear commit-section empty or unavailable copy instead of blank content or crashes
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Expected touch points include packages/cli/web/src/lib/types.ts, packages/cli/web/src/lib/api.ts, packages/cli/web/src/hooks/useQueries.ts, and IssueDetailPage.tsx. Keep Issue Detail shallow: summary and commit navigation, not inline full diff review.

tasks.title: Convert Files changed into a PR-style merge-base reader
tasks.description: Reshape `/issue/:number/files` so its default reading flow is the issue change set that will merge into base, not a generic base-vs-head browser. Update the page header, behind-base notice, toolbar hierarchy, and file rendering flow so users immediately see continuous file diffs while advanced modes remain available as secondary controls.
acceptanceCriteria: Files page header frames the branch relationship as `head wants to merge into base` and explicitly states it is showing merge-base to issue-head changes
When the issue branch is behind base, the page shows a non-blocking notice explaining that only issue-introduced changes from the merge base are displayed
The primary toolbar emphasizes PR-style reading controls such as all-commits scope, file filtering, and diff settings rather than exposing raw/full/search/commit mode as equal top-level buttons
The main reader shows a continuous file diff flow by default instead of requiring file selection before any patch content appears
Commit-specific inspection remains available as a clearly secondary mode and does not alter the default issue-level counts or merge-base semantics
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Reuse the existing diff parser, tree, and reader panes where possible. Prefer moving advanced modes into secondary settings or file-level actions over deleting the underlying capability.

tasks.title: Add semantic regression coverage for merge-base review behavior
tasks.description: Add focused backend and frontend tests that prove merge-base semantics stay correct for ahead-only and ahead-plus-behind branches, and that the UI presents the corrected counts and availability states. Cover commit navigation and the behind-base explanatory copy so future refactors cannot silently revert to polluted two-dot behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend tests cover an ahead-only branch where two-dot and three-dot results match and an ahead-plus-behind branch where merge-base diff excludes base-only files
A regression fixture equivalent to issue #199 proves the files-changed count reflects the merge-base diff instead of the polluted two-dot result
Frontend tests cover Issue Detail commit summary states and Files changed merge framing, including the behind-base explanatory notice
Frontend tests verify commit-specific inspection does not change the default issue-level file counts or summary meaning
Relevant test suites pass
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Prefer focused API and component tests over broad snapshots. Reuse the nearest existing issue diff/files test patterns and add assertions around semantic metadata, corrected counts, and unavailable states.
